nodes.description: Overall water splitting PtRu-Co₃O₄ || PtRu-Co₃O₄ in 0.5 M H₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: PtRu-Co₃O₄ exhibits remarkable catalytic activity for overall water splitting with a small voltage of 1.52 V to reach 10 mA cm⁻²... can drive a high current density of 100 mA cm⁻² at a voltage of 1.63 V... extraordinary durability... without significant performance degradation under long-term constant current density of 10 or 100 mA cm⁻² for 100 h

nodes.description: PEMWE performance as anode with Pt/C cathode
nodes.source_text: the PEM electrolyzer using PtRu-Co₃O₄ (0.23 mg_Pt+Ru cm⁻²) exhibits remarkable activity with a voltage of 1.83 V for achieving the current density of 1.0 A cm⁻²... could be operated at the current density of 200 mA cm⁻² for at least 200 h without significant performance decay
PtRu-Co₃O₄ possesses outstanding stability with no significant increase in potential at 50 mA cm⁻² during 100 h of electrolysis in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ solution
The measured Faradaic efficiency for O₂ production over the PtRu-Co₃O₄ catalyst remains at almost 100%

nodes.characterization_summary: PtRu-Co3O4 possesses the same crystal structure as cobalt spinel oxide (JCPDS NO. 76-1802) without impurities from Pt or Ru oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirm that PtRu-Co3O4 possesses the same crystal structure as cobalt spinel oxide (JCPDS NO. 76-1802) without impurities from Pt or Ru oxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtRu-Co3O4 and Ru-Co3O4 show porous nanosheet structures similar to Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of PtRu-Co3O4 (Figure 1c) and Ru-Co3O4 show porous nanosheet structures similar to those of the Co3O4 catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images and SAED patterns demonstrate the nanosheet structure of PtRu-Co3O4 with a polycrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns further demonstrate the nanosheet structure of PtRu-Co3O4 with a polycrystalline structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringe spacings of 0.289 nm and 0.249 nm assigned to (220) and (311) planes of Co3O4 in PtRu-Co3O4, broader than pure Co3O4 (0.286 and 0.243 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images show that the two lattice fringe spacings of 0.289 and 0.249 nm could be assigned to the (220) and (311) planes of Co3O4, respectively.

properties.description: Blue-toned HRTEM micrograph showing nanostructured material with lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: Contents of Pt and Ru in PtRu-Co3O4 determined to be 4.52 and 1.17 wt%, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the contents of Pt and Ru were determined to be 4.52 and 1.17 wt %, respectively, by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic ratio of Pt:Ru:O:Co is about 0.66:0.31:66.81:32.22 in PtRu-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of Pt:Ru:O:Co is about 0.66:0.31:66.81:32.22 determined by TEM energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (TEM-EDS).

nodes.characterization_summary: Line-scan EDS indicates Pt and Ru uniformly distributed in PtRu-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Line-scan energy-dispersive EDS by high-angle annular dark field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) indicated that Pt and Ru were uniformly distributed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Red-shift of A1g band in PtRu-Co3O4, Ru-Co3O4, and Pt-Co3O4 relative to Co3O4 evidences lattice expansion; Pt and Ru dopants preferentially occupy Co(III) octahedral sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The red-shift of the A1g band in the Raman spectra of PtRu-Co3O4, Ru-CO3O4, and Pt-CO3O4 relative to that of Co3O4 evidence the lattice expansion induced by Pt and Ru-substitution.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS shows Co2+/Co3+ ratios of 0.80, 0.63, and 0.59 for PtRu-Co3O4, Ru-Co3O4, and Co3O4 respectively; Ru 3p XPS of PtRu-Co3O4 exhibits decreased binding energy compared to Ru-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p XPS spectra of the PtRu-Co3O4 and Ru Co3O4 show an increase in the Co2+/Co3+ ratio after the incorporation of Pt and Ru into Co3O4 (the ratios of Co2+/Co3+ in PtRu-Co3O4, Ru-Co3O4, and Co3O4 are 0.80, 0.63, and 0.59, respectively)... Compared to that of Ru Co3O4, the Ru 3p XPS spectrum of PtRu-Co3O4 exhibits a decreased overall binding energy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge, Ru K-edge, and Pt L-edge XANES show decreased valence states of Co and Ru in PtRu-Co3O4 compared to Ru-Co3O4; Pt in oxide state between Pt foil and PtO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) was carried out to further investigate the effect of Pt doping on the electronic structures of Co and Ru in PtRu-Co3O4.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows shorter Co-O bond length, lower coordination numbers for Co-O and Co-Co in PtRu-Co3O4; Ru-O bond length 1.97 Å; Pt-O CN=2.0; confirms Pt/Ru integrated into Co3O4 lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) of PtRu-Co3O4 shows three distinct interatomic distance peaks in R space, corresponding to Co-O, octahedral Cooct-Cooct, and tetrahedral Cotet-Cotet.
